data.name: FullSyncSystemGone
data.value: This Connected System no longer exists, so there is no Full Synchronisation to preview.

data.name: FullSyncSystemDeleting
data.value: This Connected System is being deleted, so it will not be synchronised again.

data.name: FullSyncCapTooLow
data.value: A preview capped at fewer than one object would evaluate nothing. Leave the cap out to evaluate every object.

data.name: FullSyncNoRunProfile
data.value: This Connected System has no Full Synchronisation Run Profile, so a Full Synchronisation cannot be run. Create one on its Run Profiles tab, then preview it.

data.name: FullSyncDerivedFlowCycle
data.value: A Full Synchronisation would refuse to start, because the enabled derived Attribute Flows form a dependency cycle: {0}
data.comment: {0} describes the cycle, built from attribute names, and is not translated.

data.name: FullSyncCapped
data.value: This preview evaluates only the first {0} of the system's {1} objects. Its counts describe those objects, not the whole system, and a Full Synchronisation could do more than it shows.
data.comment: {0} is the cap, {1} the number of objects in the system.

data.name: DeletionSystemGone
data.value: This Connected System no longer exists, so there is no deletion to preview.

data.name: DeletionAlreadyDeleting
data.value: This Connected System is already being deleted. Part of what a preview would describe has already happened, so it cannot be previewed; its deletion Activity reports the progress.

data.name: DeletionDerivedFlowsRead
data.value: Derived flows on {0} read '{1}', which this deletion clears or changes. The deletion marks the objects affected so those flows recompute at the next synchronisation of the system hosting them; this preview shows the change to '{1}' but not the derived values that follow from it.
data.comment: {0} is a comma-separated list of Connected System names; {1} is a Metaverse Attribute name. Keep the straight quotes around {1}: the portal swaps that quoted name for an attribute chip.

data.name: DeletionDerivedFlowCycle
data.value: The remaining Synchronisation Rules' derived flows form a cycle, which Synchronised Deprovisioning refuses to run with: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the cycle's description, English text produced elsewhere.

data.name: ScopeSelectionNoPartitions
data.value: '{0}' uses a Connector that does not have partitions, so there is no partition or container selection to preview.
data.comment: {0} is a Connected System name.

data.name: ScopeSelectionNothingSelected
data.value: This selection leaves nothing for JIM to manage on this Connected System: {0}. Run Profiles cannot be executed against it, and every object already imported would be taken out of scope.
data.comment: {0} is a short diagnostic of what is selected, English text produced elsewhere.

data.name: ScopeSelectionInoperableRunProfiles
data.value: {0} Run Profile(s) target a partition this selection deselects and would be refused when run: {1}. Point them at a selected partition, or keep the partition selected.
data.comment: {0} is a count; {1} a comma-separated list of quoted Run Profile names.

data.name: ScopeSelectionContainersNotMeasured
data.value: The '{0}' Connector has containers but cannot say whether an object sits inside one, so this preview counts only what changing the partition selection would do. Container changes are not measured, and the counts below are not a complete answer.
data.comment: {0} is a Connector name.

data.name: ScopeSelectionBringsNewScope
data.value: This selection brings scope into JIM that it does not currently import. Objects JIM already holds there are counted below; objects it has never imported cannot be, because there is nothing to count until a Full Import runs and discovers them.

data.name: ActivityValidating
data.value: Validating the proposed configuration
data.comment: The preview Activity's progress message while its structural checks run.

data.name: ActivityCannotBeApplied
data.value: The proposed configuration cannot be applied

data.name: ActivityCounting
data.value: Counting affected objects

data.name: ActivityEvaluating
data.value: Evaluating what the change would do

data.name: ActivityComplete
data.value: Preview complete

data.name: ActivityCancelled
data.value: The preview was cancelled

data.name: ActivityFailedWhile
data.value: The preview failed while {0}
data.comment: {0} is one of the ActivityWhile... phrases.

data.name: ActivityWhileValidating
data.value: validating the proposed configuration
data.comment: Completes "The preview failed while ...". French: noun phrase after "pendant".

data.name: ActivityWhileCounting
data.value: counting the objects the change would affect
data.comment: Completes "The preview failed while ...". French: noun phrase after "pendant".

data.name: ActivityWhileEvaluating
data.value: evaluating what the change would do
data.comment: Completes "The preview failed while ...". French: noun phrase after "pendant".

data.name: EnglishFromElsewhere
data.comment: Carries text that is produced outside JIM.Application and is not yet a message (for instance a validator's reason). It is shown as it is, in English, until its producer is converted.

data.name: ObjectMatchingSameAsStored
data.value: The proposed Object Matching Rules match the ones this Connected System already has, so no object would join differently and no impact is counted below.

data.name: ObjectMatchingOnlyUnjoined
data.value: Object Matching Rules are evaluated only for objects that are not already joined to a Metaverse Object. Objects already joined keep the Metaverse Object they have, whatever this change does, so the impact below covers the unjoined population only.

data.name: ObjectMatchingSwitchToAdvanced
data.value: The proposal switches this Connected System to Advanced matching, so the rules held against each Connected System Object Type stop being used and each Synchronisation Rule's own rules apply instead. A Synchronisation Rule carrying no rules of its own joins nothing.

data.name: ObjectMatchingSwitchToSimple
data.value: The proposal switches this Connected System to Simple matching, so each Synchronisation Rule's own rules stop being used and the rules held against each Connected System Object Type apply instead. An Object Type carrying no rules of its own joins nothing.

data.name: ObjectMatchingTypeLeftWithNoRule
data.value: The proposal leaves '{0}' with no Object Matching Rule, so no object of that type would ever join an existing Metaverse Object. Every unjoined object would project a new identity instead, which is how duplicate identities are created.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type name, or the ObjectMatchingThisType phrase where the type is unknown.

data.name: ObjectMatchingThisType
data.value: this type
data.comment: Stands in for an Object Type's name inside quotes where the type can no longer be found.

data.name: ObjectMatchingOwnerSyncRule
data.value: a Synchronisation Rule
data.comment: Stands in for the owner's name inside quotes where the Synchronisation Rule can no longer be found.

data.name: ObjectMatchingOwnerObjectType
data.value: an Object Type
data.comment: Stands in for the owner's name inside quotes where the Object Type can no longer be found.

data.name: ObjectMatchingRuleNamed
data.value: Object Matching Rule {0} on '{1}'
data.comment: {0} is the rule's position (1 first); {1} is the Object Type or Synchronisation Rule holding it.

data.name: ObjectMatchingNoMetaverseObjectType
data.value: {0} names no Metaverse Object Type to search. Simple mode rules must name one; in Advanced mode the Synchronisation Rule supplies it.
data.comment: {0} is an ObjectMatchingRuleNamed phrase.

data.name: ObjectMatchingRuleProblem
data.comment: {0} is an ObjectMatchingRuleNamed phrase; {1} is why the rule cannot be evaluated.

data.name: ObjectMatchingTargetAttributeGone
data.value: It targets a Metaverse Attribute that no longer exists.

data.name: ObjectMatchingTypeNotInSchema
data.value: It belongs to a Connected System Object Type that is not part of this system's schema.

data.name: DirectionImport
data.value: Import
data.comment: The direction of a Synchronisation Rule, named inside a sentence.

data.name: DirectionExport
data.value: Export
data.comment: The direction of a Synchronisation Rule, named inside a sentence.

data.name: BehaviourSameSettings
data.value: The proposed settings match the ones this Synchronisation Rule already has, so nothing would change and no impact is counted below.

data.name: BehaviourDirectionImmutable
data.value: Direction cannot be changed on a saved Synchronisation Rule. This rule's Attribute Flow mappings and Object Matching Rules are written for {0}, and would all address the wrong side as {1}. Create a rule in the direction you need instead.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are DirectionImport or DirectionExport.

data.name: BehaviourEnabling
data.value: Enabling this Synchronisation Rule starts it contributing on the next synchronisation: it begins flowing its Attribute Flow mappings, and whatever it projects or provisions starts being created.

data.name: BehaviourDisabling
data.value: Disabling this Synchronisation Rule stops it contributing on the next synchronisation. Attribute values it currently owns pass to another contributor where there is one, and are kept, ready for the rule to be enabled again, where it was the only one. It stops projecting and provisioning.

data.name: BehaviourProjectOn
data.value: Turning Project To Metaverse on creates a new Metaverse Object for every in-scope object this rule manages that matches none, which is how identities are created in bulk.

data.name: BehaviourProvisionOn
data.value: Turning Provision To Connected System on creates a Connected System Object in the target system for every in-scope Metaverse Object that has none. This is object creation at scale, and the count below is how many.

data.name: BehaviourEnforceStateOff
data.value: Turning Enforce State off stops this rule correcting drift, so the objects it manages are free to diverge from what JIM holds from the moment it is saved. Nothing is corrected until it is turned back on.

data.name: BehaviourRuleDisabled
data.value: This Synchronisation Rule is disabled, so no synchronisation applies it today. The impact below describes what the next synchronisation would do once it is enabled.

data.name: BehaviourEnforceStateImportOnly
data.value: Enforce State governs drift correction on Export rules only, so changing it on this Import rule has no effect.

data.name: BehaviourProvisionExportOnly
data.value: Provision To Connected System applies to Export rules only, so changing it on this Import rule has no effect.

data.name: BehaviourProjectImportOnly
data.value: Project To Metaverse applies to Import rules only, so changing it on this Export rule has no effect.

data.name: DestructiveNoChange
data.value: Neither destructive setting changes under this proposal, so no object's fate changes and no impact is counted below.

data.name: DestructiveOutboundOnExport
data.value: The Outbound Deprovision Action is read only by export Synchronisation Rules, so changing it on this import rule changes no object's fate and is not counted below.

data.name: DestructiveInboundOnImport
data.value: The Inbound Out-of-Scope Action is read only by import Synchronisation Rules, so changing it on this export rule changes no object's fate and is not counted below.

data.name: DestructiveRuleDisabled
data.value: This Synchronisation Rule is disabled, so no synchronisation applies its settings today. The counts below describe what the next synchronisation would do once it is enabled.

data.name: DestructiveSiblingKeepsJoin
data.value: {0} also covers this object type and keeps its objects joined (Remain Joined). Where an object leaves every import Synchronisation Rule, the rules that held it decide, and Remain Joined from any of them keeps the join, so this change disconnects only objects those rules never held. The counts below include only those.
data.comment: {0} is a comma-separated list of quoted Synchronisation Rule names. Remain Joined is the name of an Inbound Out-of-Scope Action option.

data.name: DeletionSettingsNeedsAuthoritativeSource
data.value: Deleting when an authoritative source disconnects needs at least one Connected System named as an authoritative source. Without one, synchronisation falls back to deleting when the last connector disconnects, which is a different rule from the one selected.

data.name: DeletionSettingsNegativeGracePeriod
data.value: A Deletion Grace Period cannot be negative.

data.name: DeletionSettingsSourcesChanged
data.value: The authoritative sources have changed. This decides what happens the next time a Connected System Object disconnects, so it moves no Metaverse Object's deletion date today and is not counted below.

data.name: ScopingProposalSameAsStored
data.value: The proposed Scoping Criteria match the ones this Synchronisation Rule already has, so no object changes scope and no impact is counted below.

data.name: ScopingProposalRemovesEveryCriterion
data.value: The proposal removes every Scoping Criterion, so this Synchronisation Rule would manage every object of type '{0}' rather than a selected population.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type name, or the ScopingConfiguredType phrase where the type is unknown.

data.name: ScopingConfiguredType
data.value: the configured type
data.comment: Stands in for an Object Type's name inside quotes where it cannot be found.

data.name: ScopingProposalRuleDisabled
data.value: This Synchronisation Rule is disabled, so no synchronisation applies its scope today. The counts below describe what the next synchronisation would do once it is enabled.

data.name: ScopingProposalUnscopedSiblingDisconnect
data.value: Import Synchronisation Rule '{0}' covers this object type with no Scoping Criteria, so every object stays joined whatever this rule says: narrowing this rule's criteria disconnects nothing. An object that leaves this rule's scope stops receiving its Attribute Flow; under its Out-of-Scope Action, Disconnect, the values this rule contributed are handed to the rules that still cover the object.
data.comment: {0} is a Synchronisation Rule name. Disconnect is the name of an Inbound Out-of-Scope Action option.

data.name: ScopingProposalUnscopedSiblingRemainJoined
data.value: Import Synchronisation Rule '{0}' covers this object type with no Scoping Criteria, so every object stays joined whatever this rule says: narrowing this rule's criteria disconnects nothing. An object that leaves this rule's scope stops receiving its Attribute Flow; under its Out-of-Scope Action, Remain Joined, the values this rule contributed stay as they are.
data.comment: {0} is a Synchronisation Rule name. Remain Joined is the name of an Inbound Out-of-Scope Action option.

data.name: ScopingProposalExpressionReadsMetaverseOnImport
data.value: A proposed Scoping Criterion's expression reads {0}, but an import Synchronisation Rule evaluates its scope against Connected System attributes (cs["..."]), so that input would never hold a value.
data.comment: {0} is an expression accessor such as mv["name"].

data.name: ScopingProposalExpressionReadsConnectedSystemOnExport
data.value: A proposed Scoping Criterion's expression reads {0}, but an export Synchronisation Rule evaluates its scope against Metaverse Attributes (mv["..."]), so that input would never hold a value.
data.comment: {0} is an expression accessor such as cs["name"].

data.name: ScopingProposalNamesNoAttribute
data.value: A proposed Scoping Criterion names no attribute, so there is nothing for it to evaluate and it would narrow nothing.

data.name: ScopingProposalReadsMetaverseOnImport
data.value: A proposed Scoping Criterion reads a Metaverse Attribute, but an import Synchronisation Rule evaluates its scope against Connected System attributes, so the criterion would never match and the scope would be wider than it appears.

data.name: ScopingProposalReadsConnectedSystemOnExport
data.value: A proposed Scoping Criterion reads a Connected System attribute, but an export Synchronisation Rule evaluates its scope against Metaverse Attributes, so the criterion would never match and the scope would be wider than it appears.

data.name: ListAnd
data.comment: Joins two items of a list; a longer list nests it.

data.name: MetaverseAttributeNumbered
data.value: Metaverse Attribute {0}
data.comment: Stands in for an attribute's name where only its id is known. {0} is the id.

data.name: RuleNamesOne
data.value: Synchronisation Rule '{0}'
data.comment: One Synchronisation Rule named inside a sentence; {0} is its name.

data.name: RuleNamesOther
data.value: Synchronisation Rules {0}
data.comment: Several Synchronisation Rules named inside a sentence; {0} is a comma-separated list of quoted names.

data.name: AttributeFlowSameAsStored
data.value: The proposed Attribute Flow matches the mappings this Synchronisation Rule already has, so no object changes and no impact is counted below.

data.name: AttributeFlowRemovesEveryMapping
data.value: The proposal removes every mapping, so this Synchronisation Rule would flow nothing.

data.name: AttributeFlowRuleDisabled
data.value: This Synchronisation Rule is disabled, so no synchronisation applies its Attribute Flow today. The values below describe what the next synchronisation would write once it is enabled.

data.name: AttributeFlowRemovedKeepValues
data.value: The proposal removes this Synchronisation Rule's Attribute Flow to '{0}', and you chose to keep the values it contributed. They remain in place with no record of where they came from, and no synchronisation will ever recall them; no value change is counted below for them.
data.comment: {0} is a Metaverse Attribute name. Keep the straight quotes: the portal swaps that quoted name for an attribute chip.

data.name: AttributeFlowKeptAlsoWrittenBy
data.value: '{0}' is also written by {1}. The kept values remain until one of those rules next writes the attribute and wins Attribute Priority; what it would write is not counted below.
data.comment: {0} is a Metaverse Attribute name; {1} is a RuleNames phrase.

data.name: AttributeFlowRemovedRecalled
data.value: The proposal removes this Synchronisation Rule's Attribute Flow to '{0}'. The values it contributed are recalled at the next synchronisation of the contributing Connected System, Delta or Full: where another Attribute Flow also contributes the attribute its value takes over, otherwise the attribute is cleared. No value change is counted below for them, because the recall happens in that synchronisation rather than in this save.
data.comment: {0} is a Metaverse Attribute name. Keep the straight quotes: the portal swaps that quoted name for an attribute chip.

data.name: AttributeFlowRecallReElects
data.value: '{0}' is also written by {1}, so the recall re-elects among them rather than clearing the attribute; what they would write in place of the withdrawn values is not counted below.
data.comment: {0} is a Metaverse Attribute name; {1} is a RuleNames phrase.

data.name: AttributeFlowBelowPriority
data.value: The proposed mapping for '{0}' sits below {1} in Attribute Priority, so a synchronisation would evaluate it and then write nothing. Raise its priority to make it the contributor that wins the attribute.
data.comment: {0} is a Metaverse Attribute name; {1} is a RuleNames phrase.

data.name: AttributeFlowDependantMissingInput
data.value: Once this proposal is saved, the Attribute Flow to '{0}' on Synchronisation Rule '{1}' would be missing an input: it reads {2}. Its Missing Input Behaviour then decides what it writes.
data.comment: {0} is a Metaverse Attribute name; {1} a Synchronisation Rule name; {2} lists the missing inputs.

data.name: AttributeFlowMissingInputThroughDerived
data.value: '{0}', whose only remaining contributors are themselves missing an input
data.comment: Describes one missing input of a derived Attribute Flow.

data.name: AttributeFlowMissingInputNoFlow
data.value: '{0}', which would have no enabled Attribute Flow contributing it
data.comment: Describes one missing input of a derived Attribute Flow.

data.name: AttributeFlowReadsChangedDirect
data.value: reads '{0}'
data.comment: How a derived Attribute Flow relates to an attribute the proposal changes.

data.name: AttributeFlowReadsChangedThrough
data.value: depends on '{0}', through other derived attributes
data.comment: How a derived Attribute Flow relates to an attribute the proposal changes.

data.name: AttributeFlowOtherSystemReader
data.value: The Attribute Flow to '{0}' on Synchronisation Rule '{1}' {2}, which this proposal changes. It runs in that Synchronisation Rule's own Connected System, so it is re-evaluated when that Connected System next synchronises; what it would write is not counted below.
data.comment: {0} is a Metaverse Attribute name; {1} a Synchronisation Rule name; {2} is the AttributeFlowReadsChanged phrase.

data.name: AttributeFlowNoTargetAttribute
data.value: A proposed Attribute Flow mapping names no target attribute, so it has nowhere to write.

data.name: AttributeFlowWritesConnectedSystemOnImport
data.value: A proposed Attribute Flow mapping writes a Connected System attribute, but an import Synchronisation Rule flows into the Metaverse, so the mapping would write nothing.

data.name: AttributeFlowWritesMetaverseOnExport
data.value: A proposed Attribute Flow mapping writes a Metaverse Attribute, but an export Synchronisation Rule flows out to a Connected System, so the mapping would write nothing.

data.name: AttributeFlowNoSource
data.value: A proposed Attribute Flow mapping has no source, so there is no value for it to write.
